def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Boundary overcompute grows with the logarithm of tile edge waste.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    # A nearly empty final CTA wave loses useful machine throughput.
    s = s + f.tail_waste * w[1]
    # One-wave or otherwise poorly amortized grids expose scheduling startup.
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[2]
    # CTA dispatch cost is fixed per CTA, so compress its wide normalized range.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.dispatch_overhead_per_flop) * w[3]
    # Local-memory spill traffic is an especially expensive extra data path.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[4]
    # Short pipelines expose fill and drain overhead regardless of roofline regime.
    s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[5]
    # Fixed front-end work is most important when the shortest dimension cannot amortize it.
    if p.log_min_dim < 8:
        # Static instruction footprint creates instruction-cache and front-end pressure.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_cache_footprint) * w[16]
        # Absolute per-thread instructions expose fixed issue work on small tiles.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instructions_per_thread) * w[17]
        # Small internal output work leaves thread coordination poorly amortized.
        s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[18]
        # Each reduction iteration carries loop-control and synchronization work.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[19]
        # Pipeline stage timing distinguishes latency-hiding choices in the fixed-work regime.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[20]
    else:
        # The same front-end quantities are amortized differently for larger shapes.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_cache_footprint) * w[21]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instructions_per_thread) * w[22]
        s = s + f.thread_work_granularity_deficit * w[23]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.mainloop_iteration_count) * w[24]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[25]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        # In the bandwidth regime, replicated operand traffic is the primary cost.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[6]
        # Poor tile coalescing directly increases global-memory transactions.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.coalescing_stride_ratio) * w[7]
        # Lost raster locality removes cache reuse and raises memory traffic.
        s = s + f.raster_locality_deficit * w[8]
        # Low tile arithmetic intensity makes each fetched byte less productive.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[9]
        # Parallel split-K partial materialization adds bandwidth demand.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[10]
    else:
        # In the compute regime, unfilled thread slots reduce latency hiding.
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[11]
        # Register allocation pressure limits resident work and issue hiding.
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[12]
        # Instruction work per useful arithmetic competes with tensor issue slots.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[13]
        # Serial split-K dependencies reduce independent accumulator work.
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[14]
        # Extra parallel-reduction arithmetic is paid on a compute-bound path.
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[15]
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # output-boundary overwork grows multiplicatively with the tile overhang
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    # register spills cause an abrupt local-memory path
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[1]
    # the final CTA wave can leave SM capacity unused
    s = s + f.tail_waste * w[2]
    # serial split-K exposes a dependency between partial accumulations
    s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[3]
    # parallel split-K adds global partial write/read traffic
    s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[4]
    # geometric partitioning matters differently for square-like and rectangular outputs
    if p.output_aspect_imbalance < 0.5:
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.grid_aspect_imbalance) * w[5]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch) * w[6]
        s = s + f.contiguous_tile_span_deficit * w[7]
    else:
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.grid_aspect_imbalance) * w[8]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch) * w[9]
        s = s + f.contiguous_tile_span_deficit * w[10]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        # repeated operand loads are the principal bandwidth cost
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[11]
        # low-intensity CTA tiles consume bandwidth for little arithmetic
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[12]
        # a long raster reuse window reduces cache reuse
        s = s + f.raster_reuse_window_pressure * w[13]
    else:
        # wide-range front-end work competes with tensor arithmetic
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[14]
        # unfilled thread capacity reduces latency hiding
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[15]
        # register allocation pressure limits concurrent work
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[16]
        # parallel split-K also adds accumulator arithmetic in this regime
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[17]
    # Extra stages can hide operand latency only with usable alignment and a long K/workload.
    # In that regime, the stage-time axis rewards the multistage family, while
    # fill/drain and explicit extra-buffer cost remain penalties.
    if p.alignment_deficit < 0.5 and p.log_flops > 35:
        s = s + np.log2(f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[18]
        s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[19]
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.extra_pipeline_stage_count) * w[20]
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[21]
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[22]
    else:
        # Without alignment or enough work, only the resource burden of stages pays.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.extra_pipeline_stage_count) * w[23]
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[24]
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[25]
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Boundary predication: compress the wide output-tile overwork range.
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    # Last-wave idle time grows superlinearly as the surviving wave empties.
    s = s + (-np.log(np.clip(1.0 - f.tail_waste, 1.0e-6, 1.0))) * w[1]
    # Register spills are a discontinuous transition to very slow local memory.
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[2]
    # Spill severity captures the amount of local-memory traffic after that transition.
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[3]
    # Split-K partial traffic and serial accumulator round-trips add global-memory work.
    s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[4]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.serial_reduction_traffic_fraction) * w[5]
    # Serial split-K also removes independent accumulation work.
    s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[6]
    # Pipeline prologue/epilogue and stage-management cost is paid in every regime.
    s = s + np.log2(f.stage_latency_time_ratio) * w[7]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        # Below the roofline, replicated operand loads and poor coalescing consume bandwidth.
        s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[8]
        s = s + f.raster_reuse_eviction * w[9]
        s = s + f.operand_contiguity_deficit * w[10]
        # Output stores add memory transactions on the bandwidth-limited path.
        s = s + f.output_store_run_density * w[11]
        # A tile can remain bandwidth-limited even when whole-shape intensity looks adequate.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[12]
    else:
        # Above the roofline, issue overhead and resource occupancy limit tensor throughput.
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[13]
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[14]
        s = s + f.register_file_pressure * w[15]
        s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[16]
        # Poor CTA-local arithmetic intensity can reintroduce a memory bottleneck.
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[17]
        if p.output_work_per_sm > 1024:
            # On broad, saturated grids, eviction can be traded for better swizzle scheduling and reuse.
            s = s + f.raster_reuse_eviction * w[18]
            s = s + f.resident_block_scarcity * w[19]
            s = s + np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[20]
    # Shared-memory allocation is most exposed when output work is too small to amortize
    # residency losses; the scarcity interaction distinguishes the limiting resource.
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 1024:
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[21]
        s = s + f.shared_buffer_overhead_fraction * w[22]
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[23]
        # Extra staged buffering makes shared-memory pressure more consequential in multistage families.
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * f.multistage_family_indicator * w[24]
        s = s + f.shared_buffer_overhead_fraction * f.multistage_family_indicator * w[25]
    else:
        # With ample output work, shared memory chiefly limits sustained CTA residency.
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[26]
        s = s + f.shared_buffer_overhead_fraction * w[27]
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * f.resident_block_scarcity * w[28]
        s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * f.multistage_family_indicator * w[29]
        s = s + f.shared_buffer_overhead_fraction * f.multistage_family_indicator * w[30]
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    s = np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) * w[0]
    s = s + f.wave_count_deficit * w[1]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.tail_waste / np.maximum(1.0 - f.tail_waste, 1e-6)) * w[2]
    s = s + f.has_spill * w[3]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.spill_traffic_ratio) * w[4]
    s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.grid_instruction_overhead_ratio) * w[5]
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio) * w[6]
        s = s + f.tile_roofline_deficit * w[7]
        s = s + f.raster_reuse_cache_pressure * w[8]
        s = s + np.log2(f.raster_band_count) * w[12]
    else:
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.instruction_density) * w[9]
        s = s + f.occupancy_deficit * w[10]
        if p.alignment_deficit > 0.25:
            if p.log_min_dim < 5:
                s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[11]
                s = s + np.log2(f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[22]
                s = s + f.pipeline_family_overhead * w[29]
            else:
                s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[23]
                s = s + np.log2(f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[24]
                s = s + f.pipeline_family_overhead * w[30]
        else:
            if p.log_min_dim < 5:
                s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[25]
                s = s + np.log2(f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[26]
                s = s + f.pipeline_family_overhead * w[31]
            else:
                s = s + f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction * w[27]
                s = s + np.log2(f.pipeline_stage_time_ratio) * w[28]
                s = s + f.pipeline_family_overhead * w[32]
        s = s + np.log2(f.raster_band_count) * w[13]
        if p.output_work_per_sm >= 1024 and p.log_min_dim >= 5:
            s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.resident_block_scarcity / np.maximum(1.0 - f.resident_block_scarcity, 1e-6)) * (1.0 + f.wave_count_deficit) * w[33]
            s = s + f.register_file_pressure * (1.0 + f.wave_count_deficit) * w[34]
            s = s + f.resource_allocation_imbalance * (1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch / 20.0) * w[35]
            s = s + f.shared_memory_pressure * w[36]
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 1024 or p.log_min_dim < 5:
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.split_k_critical_path_ratio) * w[14]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[15]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[16]
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[17]
    else:
        s = s + np.log2(1.0 + f.split_k_critical_path_ratio) * w[18]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction * w[19]
        s = s + f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction * w[20]
        s = s + f.serial_reduction_dependency * w[21]
    return s
